question: How should you respond as a nurse if a client worries that injectable contraceptives will make her permanently barren?

options.A: Provide empathetic education explaining that fertility returns after discontinuation.
options.B: Dismiss the concern as an unimportant superstition unworthy of discussion.
options.C: Advise the client to switch immediately to permanent surgical sterilization.
options.D: Confirm that temporary infertility is a permanent risk of modern drugs.

explanation: Well done! Patient, warm counseling helps clear up myths by calmly explaining that normal fertility returns once the injection wears off.

question: What is the go-to treatment to quickly filter out dangerous levels of a heavy-duty poison like lithium?

options.A: Multiple-dose ipecac
options.B: Whole bowel irrigation
options.C: Hemodialysis
options.D: Gastric lavage

explanation: When the kidneys just can't keep up, hemodialysis steps in to act like an artificial kidney, filtering the dangerous drug straight out of the blood.

question: What is the name for an organism like a mosquito that transmits a pathogen to a human?

options.A: Capsid
options.B: Dermatophyte
options.C: Vector
options.D: Mycelium

explanation: Vectors carry infectious agents from an infected animal or person to a new host. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a pressure-mapping surface on a smart bed?

options.A: To secure the patient firmly to the mattress during seizures
options.B: To display real-time pressure points and skin breakdown risks
options.C: To keep the patient cool by pumping refrigerated water
options.D: To automatically administer topical pain medications

explanation: Pressure-mapping shows a picture of where the patient's body presses down hardest, helping you know when it's time for a turn to prevent bedsores.

question: Which environmental situation should a patient with sickle cell anaemia avoid to prevent a crisis?

options.A: High humidity during the rainy season
options.B: High-altitude travel with low oxygen levels
options.C: Bright sunlight reflecting off sandy beaches
options.D: Loud noises in crowded public marketplaces

explanation: High altitudes mean less oxygen in the air. For someone with sickle cell, low oxygen can quickly cause red blood cells to sickle, triggering a painful crisis or trouble breathing.

question: Which of the following is a frequent long-term complication of poorly treated acute osteomyelitis?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Chronic osteomyelitis

explanation: When acute bone infections are not fully eradicated, they frequently transition into long-standing chronic osteomyelitis with recurrent flare-ups. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h10)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a thorough initial prenatal booking visit?

options.A: To administer the final dose of the tetanus vaccine
options.B: To perform an emergency delivery for safety
options.C: To establish a complete baseline health and obstetric history
options.D: To finalize the birth certificate before delivery

explanation: Think of the booking visit as your complete roadmap. Gathering all her past and current health details helps you guide her safely through the rest of the pregnancy.

question: Why does the law treat young offenders differently from adult criminals?

options.A: Juveniles are completely immune to all forms of criminal prosecution
options.B: Minors possess developing brains that affect impulse control and judgment
options.C: Prisons are entirely unsuitable for holding individuals under twenty
options.D: Young offenders never commit violent crimes that harm society

explanation: Great thinking! Teen brains are still growing, which means they sometimes struggle with impulse control. The justice system recognizes this and focuses more on guidance.

question: Why must you strictly tell a patient who just had transsphenoidal surgery NOT to blow their nose?

options.A: It triggers terrible allergic reactions to the nasal packing materials.
options.B: It pushes air into the ear tubes and causes permanent deafness.
options.C: It increases pressure inside the head and can ruin the surgical seal.
options.D: It causes too much mucus to form and blocks the sinus completely.

explanation: Blowing your nose spikes intracranial pressure. That sudden pressure can pop the tissue patch the surgeon placed over the surgical site, causing cerebrospinal fluid to leak out.

question: What type of air pressure is kept inside the operating room to stop outside air from rushing in when doors open?

options.A: Positive pressure
options.B: Negative pressure
options.C: Variable pressure
options.D: Neutral pressure

explanation: Positive pressure acts like an invisible shield, pushing air outward when doors open so germs stay out of the sterile theatre. Well done!

question: Which principle of intersectoral collaboration focuses on putting the most vulnerable people first?

options.A: Specialization
options.B: Privatization
options.C: Equity
options.D: Centralization

explanation: You've got it! Equity means fairness—making sure resources and care reach the people who need them the most, rather than just splitting everything equally.

question: What is the main job of follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in males?

options.A: Supporting sperm production in the Sertoli cells
options.B: Producing secondary sex characteristics in muscle
options.C: Triggering the release of gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.D: Controlling the contraction of the prostate gland

explanation: FSH works directly on the Sertoli cells in the testes to help nourish and build healthy sperm cells. Keep up the great studying!

question: Why is it unsafe to change the needle but keep using the same syringe barrel for another injection?

options.A: New needles never fit securely onto used plastic syringe tips
options.B: The plastic material of the barrel melts when exposed to air twice
options.C: The fluid path and internal parts of the syringe are already contaminated
options.D: The second medication will chemically react and turn into a solid block

explanation: Once a needle touches a patient or medication vial, the inside of the syringe barrel is no longer sterile. Don't risk it!

question: What attitude should you always show when counseling a client who needs emergency contraception?

options.A: Skeptical and demanding proof
options.B: Non-judgmental and confidential
options.C: Public and sharing with family
options.D: Strictly moralizing and formal

explanation: As nurses, our job is to provide a safe, private, and judgment-free space so clients feel comfortable seeking help without fear of stigma. Excellent nursing values!

question: Your patient is prescribed sucralfate along with other oral medications. How should you time their doses?

options.A: Give sucralfate immediately after meals alongside all other pills
options.B: Mix all drugs into the same liquid suspension for convenience
options.C: Crush all medications together and administer them simultaneously
options.D: Separate sucralfate and other oral drugs by at least two hours

explanation: Because sucralfate forms a sticky coating, it can trap other drugs and stop your body from absorbing them. Give other meds a 2-hour window!

question: How does research directly help you practice evidence-based care on the ward?

options.A: It dictates the exact salary scale for nursing staff
options.B: It eliminates all documentation requirements for nurses
options.C: It replaces the need to assess individual patient preferences
options.D: It provides tested proof of which clinical interventions work best

explanation: Correct! Research gives us the reliable facts we need to update our daily ward procedures and get better results for our patients.

question: A hospital director in Lagos wants to start primary nursing on a busy surgical ward. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ensure an adequate mix of registered staff and provide training on clinical autonomy.
options.B: Fire all doctors on the ward to give nurses complete control over the hospital.
options.C: Reduce the number of visiting hours to zero minutes per day.
options.D: Ban patients from asking questions about their medications.

explanation: To make primary nursing work, management must first ensure there are enough qualified nurses and empower them to make independent clinical decisions.

question: A nurse wants to improve child immunization rates in a rural town. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Handing out flyers written in a foreign language nobody speaks
options.B: Ordering all parents to bring children to the clinic without explanation
options.C: Partnering with local religious and community leaders to promote the clinic
options.D: Closing local markets until every child receives a vaccination

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with trusted local leaders builds instant trust and encourages parents to bring their children.

question: A patient with a history of heavy drinking suddenly looks confused and has trouble moving their eyes. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Alzheimer dementia
options.B: Korsakoff syndrome
options.C: Wernicke encephalopathy
options.D: Parkinson disease

explanation: That classic mix of confusion, eye movement problems, and a history of heavy alcohol use is a textbook warning sign for acute Wernicke encephalopathy.

question: What is the first step in conducting any cross-sectional study?

options.A: Defining the research question
options.B: Publishing the results in a journal
options.C: Analyzing the final statistics
options.D: Discharging the participating patients

explanation: Every great nursing project starts with a clear question. Once you know what you're asking, the path forward becomes much easier!

question: Why are imaging studies like an MRI necessary after finding high hormone levels in the blood?

options.A: To replace the need for baseline blood work entirely
options.B: To locate the physical source or tumor causing the problem
options.C: To measure the exact daily urine output of the patient
options.D: To check if the patient has a secondary bacterial infection

explanation: Blood tests prove a hormone is too high, but imaging helps find the exact spot, like a pituitary tumor, driving the overproduction. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h4)

question: A persistently high maternal mortality ratio in a specific region most strongly points to which underlying issue?

options.A: A cultural preference for giving birth during the rainy season
options.B: Weaknesses or failures within the local emergency healthcare system
options.C: An unusually high rate of twin and triplet births in the community
options.D: Excessive availability of free antenatal care medications

explanation: When maternal mortality stays high, it usually points to poor access to skilled birth attendants, delayed referrals, and inadequate emergency care. Recognizing this helps us know where to fix the system!

question: What is the best way for nurses to physically handle needles during a count?

options.A: Glance quickly over the tray from a distance
options.B: Count only the full packs without opening them
options.C: Let the surgeon handle the items alone
options.D: Point to or touch each item individually as it is counted

explanation: You've got it! Touching or pointing to each item helps ensure nothing gets skipped. Safety first! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h4)

question: A patient comes back two days after an abscess drainage with a fever and redness that is spreading outward from the wound. What does this mean?

options.A: Worsening infection requiring prompt medical reassessment
options.B: An allergic reaction to the cotton inside the dressing
options.C: Successful eradication of all bacteria from the body
options.D: Normal healing response as the deep tissues close

explanation: Spreading redness and fever are warning signs that the infection is fighting back and traveling further. The patient needs a doctor to take a look right away.

question: What is the main focus of community nutrition compared to hospital dietetics?

options.A: Promoting health for entire populations
options.B: Managing surgical recovery diets
options.C: Treating rare genetic disorders
options.D: Prescribing weight loss pills

explanation: Community nutrition looks at whole populations to prevent health problems, while hospital dietetics focuses on treating individual patients. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h1)

question: What unit of measurement is commonly used to express energy expenditure in human nutrition?

options.A: Centimeters
options.B: Kilocalories
options.C: Milligrams
options.D: Milliliters

explanation: Energy in human nutrition is measured in kilocalories, which people commonly call calories. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h1)

question: What is a major job of international groups like the FAO in the food chain?

options.A: Directly managing hospital nutrition wards during health crises
options.B: Owning and operating all commercial farms in developing nations
options.C: Monitoring global agricultural production and issuing early famine warnings
options.D: Setting retail prices for grocery stores in local communities

explanation: Organizations like the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) keep an eye on crop conditions worldwide so they can warn countries before a famine hits.

question: Why do clients with inherited degenerative disorders need a team of different specialists (multidisciplinary team)?

options.A: Hospital regulations require at least five different specialists for every chronic illness.
options.B: It lowers the cost of hospital care by eliminating the need for registered nurses.
options.C: The disease progressively affects multiple body systems, requiring diverse specialized expertise.
options.D: Specialists can completely cure the genetic mutation if they work together.

explanation: As different body systems break down over time, various health professionals are needed to team up for physical, nutritional, and emotional support.

question: A patient is worried that eating fats will only make them gain weight. How can you best explain the good side of fats?

options.A: Fats replace water in cells during dehydration
options.B: Fats are the only nutrient that can build muscle tissue
options.C: Fats protect vital organs and help absorb certain vitamins
options.D: Fats prevent the breakdown of proteins into glucose

explanation: Well done! Dietary fats aren't just about storage; they insulate our organs and are essential for absorbing key vitamins like A, D, E, and K.

question: How do sperm travel upward through the long vas deferens during ejaculation?

options.A: By beating their flagella very rapidly
options.B: By suction created by the prostate gland
options.C: By smooth muscle peristaltic contractions
options.D: By gravity pulling them down into the urethra

explanation: Just like food moves down your gut, the walls of the vas deferens use wave-like muscle squeezes (peristalsis) to push sperm smoothly along their journey.

question: Why must a nurse check for an official agency registration number on a drug before giving it?

options.A: To determine which pharmaceutical company manufactured the raw chemical compound
options.B: To calculate the exact wholesale profit margin for the hospital pharmacy
options.C: To ensure the medication qualifies for international shipping exemptions
options.D: To confirm that the drug has been evaluated for safety, quality, and efficacy

explanation: That registration number is your safety green light! It tells you NFDAC or the relevant body has tested the drug and approved it for use.

question: How does health education in the community help reduce malaria cases?

options.A: It empowers families to use preventive tools and seek early testing
options.B: It replaces the need for hospital laboratories in rural zones
options.C: It provides immediate immunity to newborns in endemic regions
options.D: It permanently eliminates mosquito breeding sites nationwide

explanation: Well done! Teaching families how to use nets properly and report fevers early stops infections before they spiral out of control.

question: What is the best way for community health nurses to help stop unsafe abortions?

options.A: Reporting patients who come in with abortion complications
options.B: Increasing police patrols around illegal clinics
options.C: Promoting education and easy access to family planning
options.D: Banning the sale of common pain relievers

explanation: Stopping unintended pregnancies before they happen through education and contraception is the absolute best way to beat unsafe abortion. Well reasoned!

question: Why should a patient stay sitting upright for about 30 minutes after eating?

options.A: To allow the nurse enough time to clear the bedside table
options.B: To prevent food reflux and reduce the risk of aspiration
options.C: To encourage the patient to fall into a deep sleep
options.D: To help the digestive enzymes break down fats faster

explanation: Staying upright gives the stomach a head start on digesting, stopping food or acid from creeping back up into the throat.

question: On a partograph, what does crossing the alert line tell the nurse?

options.A: All interventions must be stopped immediately.
options.B: The baby has already been successfully delivered.
options.C: The mother is entering the third stage of labour.
options.D: Labour is slower than normal and requires close monitoring or referral.

explanation: Correct! The alert line is your early warning bell telling you to pay closer attention because progress is slowing down.

question: Which of these is NOT a common side effect of chemotherapy that nurses watch out for?

options.A: Permanent tissue encapsulation
options.B: Severe fatigue
options.C: Increased infection risk
options.D: Bone marrow suppression

explanation: You've got this! Encapsulation is a trait of benign, harmless-looking growths, not a side effect of chemo. Chemo hits fast-dividing cells, which often leads to fatigue and low blood counts.

question: What chemical bond in the cystine molecule do cystine-binding thiol drugs break apart?

options.A: Ionic bond
options.B: Peptide bond
options.C: Disulfide bond
options.D: Hydrogen bond

explanation: Thiol medications act like molecular scissors, specifically targeting and cutting the disulfide bond that holds the cystine molecule together. Clever, right?

question: A nurse wants to improve contraceptive acceptance in a traditional village. Which strategy is best?

options.A: Insulting the village traditions during public gatherings
options.B: Writing all health instructions in Latin
options.C: Banning husbands from attending health education talks
options.D: Engaging local community and religious leaders as health allies

explanation: Brilliant! Partnering with respected community figures builds immediate trust and helps lower resistance to reproductive health programs.

question: What usually causes bleeding inside the skull during severe fetal moulding?

options.A: High blood pressure caused by maternal pushing
options.B: Lack of vitamin K in the newborn circulation
options.C: Stretching and tearing of bridging veins inside the skull
options.D: Rupture of scalp arteries from vacuum suction

explanation: Spot on. When the skull bones overlap too severely, they stretch and strain the tiny veins inside, causing them to tear and bleed.

question: As a nurse preparing a mother for discharge, what is one of your most important responsibilities?

options.A: Ensuring the mother can name critical danger signs for herself and the baby
options.B: Confirming that lochia has completely stopped entirely
options.C: Scheduling permanent sterilization procedures before she leaves
options.D: Providing enough formula for the first three months of life

explanation: Before anyone goes home, we must make sure they know the warning signs to watch for so they can run back to the hospital if something goes wrong. Excellent safety practice! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h9)

question: What do we call the solid, mulberry-like cluster of cells formed during early embryonic travel?

options.A: Pronucleus
options.B: Zygote
options.C: Morula
options.D: Blastocyst

explanation: Spot on! The morula is a solid little cluster of cells that looks a bit like a tiny mulberry as it travels down the tube.

question: What is the medical term for coughing up blood-stained sputum?

options.A: Hemoptysis
options.B: Melena
options.C: Hematemesis
options.D: Epistaxis

explanation: Coughing up blood from the lungs is called hemoptysis. It's one of those classic signs in clinical wards that always catches a nurse's attention!

question: Why do doctors check thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and prolactin when investigating missed periods?

options.A: They measure the exact amount of blood stored in the uterine lining
options.B: Thyroid and pituitary disorders commonly disrupt normal reproductive hormones
options.C: They confirm whether the patient has an anatomical outflow blockage
options.D: They show if the ovaries have completely run out of egg follicles

explanation: Issues with your thyroid or high prolactin can easily mess up the delicate hormone signals needed for a regular period.

question: Why do clinics keep a 'buffer stock' of essential drugs?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory export quotas for foreign hospitals
options.B: To hide expired medications away from visiting inspectors
options.C: To prevent running out of drugs during unexpected supply delays
options.D: To increase the financial cost of routine patient treatments

explanation: Exactly! Think of buffer stock as your safety net so the clinic never runs dry when shipments are delayed.

question: Which of these is a common physical sign of andropause?

options.A: Complete sterility
options.B: Severe ovarian atrophy
options.C: Increased visceral fat
options.D: Permanent voice deepening

explanation: As testosterone dips, men often notice changes in their body shape, such as building up a bit more belly fat and losing some muscle firmness.

question: Why are animal bite wounds often left open at first instead of being stitched up right away?

options.A: To make it easier for the patient to apply daily bandages
options.B: To prevent trapping bacteria and reducing the risk of deep infection
options.C: To let the underlying bone heal before skin closure
options.D: To allow the skin to grow back faster without scarring

explanation: If you stitch up a dirty bite right away, you trap nasty bacteria inside. Leaving it open helps prevent painful abscesses.

question: Why do nurses view gender-based violence as a public health issue rather than just a private family matter?

options.A: Because hospitals are legally required to arrest the perpetrators immediately
options.B: Because the government funds all counseling services directly through health budgets
options.C: Because private family matters are completely outside the scope of nursing ethics
options.D: Because it causes widespread physical and mental harm requiring medical intervention

explanation: Spot on! Because abuse inflicts deep physical and emotional trauma on individuals and communities, nurses must treat it as a critical health priority.

question: A patient struggles with English, and her young son offers to translate for you. What is the best thing to do?

options.A: Use hand gestures instead of words to avoid needing any translation.
options.B: Accept the son's help immediately to save time on the ward.
options.C: Ask another nurse who is busy with medication to translate.
options.D: Request a certified medical interpreter to ensure accurate translation.

explanation: Correct! Certified interpreters keep things confidential and medically accurate, whereas family members might leave out important details.

question: When doing nursing research, what are the three main levels used to group literature sources?

options.A: Primary, secondary, and tertiary sources
options.B: Published, unpublished, and grey sources
options.C: Clinical, historical, and theoretical sources
options.D: Qualitative, quantitative, and mixed sources

explanation: You've got this! We group literature into three tiers based on how close the information is to the original study. Primary, secondary, and tertiary keep our research organized.

question: You advise a recovering patient to make half their plate colorful fruits and veggies. Which food group are you focusing on?

options.A: Energy-giving foods
options.B: Body-building foods
options.C: Perishable foods
options.D: Protective foods

explanation: Fantastic! Fruits and vegetables are our protective foods, loaded with vitamins and antioxidants to keep the body defended and healing nicely.

question: Why is it unhelpful to just write off a family planning defaulter as simply 'uncooperative'?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never return to the facility
options.B: It breaks hospital regulations regarding patient confidentiality
options.C: It automatically makes the client pregnant within a week
options.D: It ignores practical barriers and personal reasons driving the missed appointment

explanation: People miss appointments for real reasons—like side effects, transport costs, or busy schedules. Looking past the label helps us solve the actual problem together.

question: What makes patient participation in a nursing research study ethical?

options.A: It must be mandatory for all patients admitted to the ward
options.B: It must offer large financial rewards to guarantee compliance
options.C: It must be completely voluntary with informed consent
options.D: It must be approved by senior nursing staff without patient input

explanation: Spot on! Patients must always be fully informed and freely choose to join—no forcing allowed in nursing research!

question: A patient cannot move their left eye outward. Which cranial nerve nucleus in the pons is likely involved?

options.A: Trochlear nucleus
options.B: Abducens nucleus
options.C: Oculomotor nucleus
options.D: Facial nucleus

explanation: The abducens nerve (CN VI) controls the lateral rectus muscle, which pulls the eye outward. Clinical neurology made simple!

question: Why do traditional health facilities often fail to meet the needs of teenagers?

options.A: They do not have enough medical equipment for diagnosing infections
options.B: They are only open during school hours every day
options.C: They charge too much money compared to private pharmacies
options.D: They are usually structured for adults or young children rather than teenagers

explanation: Standard clinics are typically designed for adults or young children, which makes the environment intimidating for adolescents seeking care. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h1)

question: When should you release the pulled skin tissue when doing a Z-track injection?

options.A: Immediately before pushing the plunger down
options.B: Before cleansing the skin site with an alcohol swab
options.C: After the needle has been completely withdrawn
options.D: While the needle is still inside the muscle tissue

explanation: Keep holding that skin until the needle is completely out! Letting go only after the needle is gone ensures the track zips shut and traps the medicine inside.

question: When is a nurse most likely to use the rectal route of medication administration?

options.A: When the patient has severe vomiting and cannot swallow pills
options.B: When the patient prefers taking sweet liquids over tablets
options.C: When the drug is only available in a chewable tablet form
options.D: When the patient needs a slow-release oral multivitamin

explanation: Vomiting prevents oral medications from staying down, so the rectal route bypasses the upper gastrointestinal tract entirely. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h1)

question: An adult female patient refuses a procedure, but her husband insists you must do it anyway. What should you do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately without explanation
options.B: Obey the husband because he is the head of the household
options.C: Respect the patient's autonomous refusal and maintain her confidentiality
options.D: Perform the procedure secretly without the patient knowing

explanation: Every competent adult has the final say over her own body. A patient's right to refuse always overrides outside family demands. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is a leading cause of breakthrough seizures in patients with a known diagnosis?

options.A: Drinking too much water
options.B: Walking in cold weather
options.C: Eating green vegetables
options.D: Missed medication doses

explanation: Failing to take anti-seizure drugs as prescribed allows drug levels in the blood to drop, making a seizure much more likely. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h4)

question: What is the main job of a pharmacological antagonist?

options.A: It replaces the liver enzymes completely
options.B: It mimics the exact action of a natural hormone
options.C: It stimulates maximum receptor activity
options.D: It blocks the effect of an agonist

explanation: Think of an antagonist as a blocker! It attaches to a cell receptor site without turning it on, which stops agonists from coming in and doing their thing. You've got this!

question: A patient with severe nephrotic syndrome is most likely to report which initial pattern of swelling?

options.A: Severe swelling limited to the toes
options.B: Sudden swelling of only the right hand
options.C: Puffiness around the eyes upon waking up
options.D: Throbbing pain and swelling in the jaw

explanation: Periorbital edema is a classic early sign of fluid shifting into loose facial tissues overnight while the patient is lying flat. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h3)

question: What kind of thread is normally used when stitching up a perineal tear?

options.A: Non-absorbable silk sutures
options.B: Permanent nylon threads
options.C: Absorbable synthetic sutures
options.D: Stainless steel wire staples

explanation: We use absorbable sutures because they dissolve naturally in the body on their own—no painful removal appointment needed!

question: What kind of skin graft uses skin taken from another part of the patient's own body?

options.A: Xenograft
options.B: Autograft
options.C: Heterograft
options.D: Allograft

explanation: Auto means self! An autograft uses the patient's own skin so their body won't reject it. Smart healing science!

question: What happens inside the eye of a person with cataracts?

options.A: The natural lens becomes cloudy and blocks clear light
options.B: The macula breaks down and destroys central vision
options.C: Intraocular pressure rises and damages the optic nerve
options.D: Tiny blood vessels on the retina burst and bleed

explanation: Cataracts are characterized by the opacification or clouding of the eye's natural lens, which blurs the incoming light. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which part of the brain houses the front sections (anterior horns) of the lateral ventricles?

options.A: Frontal lobes
options.B: Occipital lobes
options.C: Temporal lobes
options.D: Cerebellar lobes

explanation: Spot on! The front part of the lateral ventricle reaches forward right into the frontal lobe of the brain.

question: What does a survivor-centric approach in nursing care prioritize above all else?

options.A: Public awareness campaigns in local newspapers
options.B: The survivor's rights, wishes, safety, and confidentiality
options.C: The hospital's administrative reporting deadlines
options.D: Immediate arrest of the suspect regardless of consent

explanation: A survivor-centric model puts the autonomy and emotional safety of the patient at the center of every decision. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h6)

question: In the very first hour after delivery (the fourth stage), how often should you check the mother's vital signs and womb tone?

options.A: Every 4 hours
options.B: Every 15 minutes
options.C: Every 5 minutes
options.D: Every hour

explanation: Keep shining! Because the risk of bleeding is highest right after birth, we monitor her closely every 15 minutes during that first hour.

question: What is the very first emergency medication to give someone having a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis)?

options.A: Oral antihistamine
options.B: Epinephrine
options.C: Paracetamol syrup
options.D: Normal saline IV

explanation: Epinephrine is a lifesaver! It works fast to open airways and boost low blood pressure during severe allergic reactions.

question: What simple trick involves writing off-topic discussion points on a separate board to address later?

options.A: The handover method
options.B: The delegation strategy
options.C: The parking lot technique
options.D: The triage protocol

explanation: The 'parking lot' captures unrelated or premature ideas so they don't derail the current meeting.

question: What is the main job of the lactiferous sinuses when a mother is breastfeeding?

options.A: They produce the hormone prolactin for milk synthesis
options.B: They filter waste products out of the breast milk
options.C: They secrete lubricating oils to protect the areola
options.D: They temporarily store milk before it reaches the nipple

explanation: Think of lactiferous sinuses as little holding pools right under the dark part of the breast (areola). They keep milk ready right where the baby can easily draw it out.

question: A ward has a lead time of five days for syringes. What does this lead time actually mean?

options.A: It takes five days from placing the order until the syringes arrive on the ward
options.B: The ward will completely run out of all syringes in exactly five days
options.C: Syringes on the shelf will expire and spoil after five days of storage
options.D: Nurses must count the physical syringes every five days without fail

explanation: Lead time is the delivery window required for processing, packing, and transporting ordered goods to the requesting unit. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h3)

question: Which specific nerve fibers in the skin are responsible for sending itch signals to the brain?

options.A: Pacinian touch receptors
options.B: Unmyelinated C-fibers
options.C: Meissner corpuscle endings
options.D: Large myelinated A-alpha fibers

explanation: Unmyelinated C-fibers are specialized nerve endings in our skin that pick up itch (pruritic) signals and carry them to the spinal cord.

question: What is the normal environment of the vagina in a healthy woman of childbearing age?

options.A: Acidic
options.B: Neutral
options.C: Alkaline
options.D: Variable

explanation: You're right! Friendly bacteria called lactobacilli keep the vagina acidic to protect it from bad germs and infections.

question: What is a major economic barrier to healthcare access for many low-income families in Nigeria?

options.A: An excessive abundance of free community health centers
options.B: Strict government bans on traditional herbal medicines
options.C: Out-of-pocket payment for medical services and medications
options.D: Mandatory international health insurance for all citizens

explanation: Without broad health insurance, many families have to pay cash directly for consultations, labs, and drugs, which can be tough.

question: When caring for a survivor of sexual assault, what should be the primary focus of the nurse during the physical assessment?

options.A: Focusing entirely on gathering legal evidence without offering comfort
options.B: Finishing the examination as fast as possible regardless of patient consent
options.C: Preventing re-traumatization while providing compassionate, trauma-informed care
options.D: Convincing the patient to forget the event and return home immediately

explanation: Trauma-informed care prioritizes the patient's emotional safety, consent, and control to avoid causing further psychological harm during the exam. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h4)

question: Why is using an AED as quickly as possible so important during cardiac arrest?

options.A: It automatically contacts the local police department for help
options.B: It permanently cures any underlying heart disease causing the arrest
options.C: It replaces the need to ever perform chest compressions
options.D: Survival rates drop significantly with every minute that defibrillation is delayed

explanation: Every single minute counts! Without blood flow, the brain quickly loses oxygen, so acting fast truly saves lives.

question: Why are hip and spine fractures very common in elderly patients with weakened bones?

options.A: These bones are made entirely of cartilage instead of bone.
options.B: These regions contain high amounts of fragile cancellous bone.
options.C: These bones are never protected by muscle tissue.
options.D: These areas never undergo normal bone remodeling.

explanation: Areas like the hip, wrist, and spine are packed with delicate cancellous (spongy) bone. When someone develops osteoporosis, these spongy areas lose their strength first, making them prime spots for fractures.

question: Why is it important to rest your fingers against the patient's cheek while holding the otoscope?

options.A: To block out bright room lighting for a clearer visual field
options.B: To prevent injury to the ear canal if the patient suddenly moves
options.C: To keep the otoscope battery handle from becoming disconnected
options.D: To warm up the speculum before it touches the sensitive skin

explanation: Bracing your hand on their cheek is a brilliant safety trick. If the patient jerks or moves, your hand moves with them, protecting the delicate ear canal!

question: Why do patients taking anticholinergics often end up with constipation?

options.A: Abdominal muscles become paralyzed by the drug
options.B: The medication slows down gastrointestinal motility
options.C: The drug pulls water directly out of the stool
options.D: Bile production in the liver is completely stopped

explanation: Just like it slows down the bladder, the drug also slows down movement in the gut. Less movement means sluggish bowels!

question: A 15-year-old first-time pregnant mother at 36 weeks comes in with a severe headache, blurry vision, and high blood pressure. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Acute gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.C: Chronic adult migraine headaches
options.D: Normal physiological changes of late pregnancy

explanation: Teenage mothers have a higher risk of high blood pressure disorders during pregnancy, which often show up as severe headaches, vision changes, and high BP readings.

question: Which communication channel is best suited for building deep trust and allowing immediate feedback with a patient?

options.A: A prerecorded radio jingle
options.B: Interpersonal communication
options.C: A national television advertisement
options.D: A billboard on a major highway

explanation: Nothing beats face-to-face talk! Interpersonal communication lets you clear doubts, answer questions directly, and build wonderful rapport with your patients.

question: Why is it important to celebrate small wins openly during a long-term project?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory government public relations laws
options.B: To maintain team momentum and prevent burnout
options.C: To distract staff from ongoing clinical errors on the ward
options.D: To permanently end all team meetings and project work

explanation: You got it! Shouting out small victories keeps everyone motivated and reminds the team that their hard work is making a difference.

question: Long before modern labs, how did early humans figure out which foods were safe to eat?

options.A: Microscopic testing
options.B: Written government guidelines
options.C: Trial and error
options.D: Chemical analysis

explanation: Spot on! Before science labs, our ancestors had to rely on simple observation and trying things out to see what was safe to put in their bodies.

question: A young, single mother is struggling with depression, debt, and a crying baby with colic. What should the nurse conclude?

options.A: The family has multiple overlapping risk factors for potential maltreatment
options.B: Depression in mothers has no proven link to child neglect
options.C: The infant is safe because colic is a temporary developmental stage
options.D: Financial debt is the sole driver of abuse in this household

explanation: Young age, mental stress, money troubles, and a fussy baby pile up to create high risk. This family needs extra support!

question: When should a nurse document that a medication has been given?

options.A: Before going to prepare the medication in the treatment room
options.B: Immediately after administering the medication to the patient
options.C: Before checking the patient's identity band on the bed
options.D: At the end of the entire nursing shift for all patients combined

explanation: Documentation must happen right after giving the drug to prevent accidental double-dosing and maintain an accurate medical record. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h2)

question: Biological sex is primarily determined by which of the following?

options.A: The cultural expectations placed on a child by family
options.B: How a person presents themselves in the community
options.C: The type of clothing a person chooses to wear
options.D: Anatomical and physiological traits like chromosomes

explanation: Biological sex relates to physical markers such as chromosomes, hormones, and reproductive organs rather than social or cultural factors. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is a major safety risk when dealing with pressurized gas cylinders as waste?

options.A: Gradual chemical corrosion of plastic containers
options.B: Spread of bacterial infections through the air
options.C: Risk of explosion when exposed to high heat
options.D: Attraction of radioactive dust particles

explanation: Pressurized containers can blow up violently if they get tossed into an incinerator or face extreme heat. Safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h6)

question: How can nurses directly help reduce the problem of under-prescription?

options.A: By replacing missing physician orders with over-the-counter remedies
options.B: By advocating for evidence-based treatments during multidisciplinary rounds
options.C: By writing independent prescriptions for specialized cardiac drugs
options.D: By discharging patients early when medications are unavailable

explanation: You got it! Because nurses spend the most time with patients, they are in the best position to spot missing therapies and speak up during team meetings.

question: How is an idiosyncratic reaction different from a regular side effect?

options.A: It occurs in only a small number of people regardless of dose
options.B: It only happens when a patient takes an overdose of medicine
options.C: It can be accurately predicted using standard body weight formulas
options.D: It always involves a classic skin rash and itching

explanation: Unlike common side effects that happen to lots of people, idiosyncratic reactions are rare and don't care about the dose size. Great job thinking this through!

question: A patient with a history of heart attacks is discharged without being given a statin or beta-blocker. What is this patient at higher risk for?

options.A: Immediate kidney failure caused by excessive medication
options.B: Acute drug toxicity from an accidental double dose
options.C: Severe antibiotic resistance from prolonged drug exposure
options.D: A recurrent cardiac event due to lack of secondary prevention

explanation: Brilliant! Leaving out essential recovery drugs (secondary prevention) significantly increases the chance that the patient might suffer another heart attack or stroke.

question: What is a normal finding right after Gallows traction is removed?

options.A: Complete loss of feeling in both legs
options.B: One leg suddenly growing longer than the other
options.C: Running and walking right away without help
options.D: Stiffness in the hips and knees from lying still

explanation: Keeping those little legs up in the air for weeks makes the joints stiff. Gentle stretching and movement will get them back to normal in no time!

question: A patient tells you they are too busy with work and transport to visit the gym. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Tell them that exercise is optional if they take their blood pressure medication
options.B: Advise them to stop working so hard and prioritize leisure time instead
options.C: Suggest simple physical activities that can be built directly into daily chores and routines
options.D: Insist that they must find time for a structured gym membership every evening

explanation: Brilliant! Health advice has to be practical. Recommending things like walking more or active housework fits right into their busy schedules without costing extra money.

question: What is the primary reason harmful traditional practices persist in many communities?

options.A: Mandates from international health bodies
options.B: Lack of available modern medical drugs
options.C: Direct enforcement by government laws
options.D: Deeply rooted cultural and social beliefs

explanation: These practices survive because communities view them as long-standing traditions tied to identity and social acceptance. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h1)

question: Which of these is a very common skin sign of an adverse drug reaction?

options.A: High fever with muscle stiffness
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the urine
options.C: Hives and generalized skin itching
options.D: Sudden swelling of the knee joints

explanation: Spotting rashes, hives (urticaria), and itchy skin is often the first visible clue that a patient is reacting badly to a drug.

question: What is a common misconception about advance care planning in healthcare?

options.A: That patients must pay a fee to create an advance directive
options.B: That doctors must approve every sentence written in a living will
options.C: That it is just a one-time signature on a legal form rather than an ongoing conversation
options.D: That nurses are legally forbidden from talking about living wills

explanation: Advance care planning is a continuous process of communication between patients, families, and providers, not just paperwork. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why are professional boundaries so important in nursing?

options.A: They protect both the patient and the nurse from role confusion
options.B: They ensure the nurse never has to show empathy to anyone
options.C: They prevent patients from asking questions about medications
options.D: They allow the nurse to ignore hospital policies safely

explanation: Exactly! Boundaries keep the care safe, clear, and strictly focused on the patient's recovery.

question: Which group of vegetables is famous for helping your liver clear out toxins?

options.A: Cruciferous vegetables
options.B: Root and tuber vegetables
options.C: Fruiting vegetables
options.D: Leafy green vegetables

explanation: Spot on! Vegetables like cabbage and broccoli belong to the cruciferous family and contain special compounds that give your liver a helping hand.

question: During a hysterosalpingography (HSG) procedure, what is injected into the uterus to make the tubes visible on an X-ray?

options.A: Sterile normal saline
options.B: Liquid medical silicone
options.C: Radioactive glucose solution
options.D: Radiopaque contrast dye

explanation: Doctors use a special contrast dye so that X-ray machines can clearly trace the fluid as it flows through the womb and down the fallopian tubes.

question: What do we call a failure to use ordinary care that a reasonable nurse would show, resulting in patient harm?

options.A: Advocacy
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Negligence
options.D: Battery

explanation: Correct! Negligence is basically careless nursing—failing to act with the standard of care expected, leading to accidental harm.

question: A patient wants to eat more fiber without getting severe gas and bloating. What advice should you give?

options.A: Introduce high-fiber foods slowly so the digestive system can adapt over time.
options.B: Take strong laxatives with every single meal containing fiber.
options.C: Stop eating all forms of fiber completely to avoid any digestive effort.
options.D: Eat a massive amount of beans and raw vegetables all at once on day one.

explanation: Slow and steady wins the race! Giving the gut time to adjust to fiber prevents sudden cramps and gas.

question: What is the main superpower of community herd immunity?

options.A: Reducing the cost of hospital building construction
options.B: Protecting vulnerable individuals who cannot be vaccinated
options.C: Eliminating the need for clean water and sanitation
options.D: Ensuring every adult receives an annual booster shot

explanation: When most people around are immunized, it builds a protective shield around babies or sick individuals who cannot take vaccines yet. Brilliant concept to master!

question: According to the Swiss Cheese Model, what usually causes patient harm?

options.A: A combination of multiple small system failures
options.B: Unavoidable natural deterioration of medical tools
options.C: Sudden refusal of treatment by the patient's family
options.D: Intentional sabotage by a single disgruntled worker

explanation: Errors usually happen when several safety checks fail all at the same time, letting a mistake reach the patient.

question: Why is it best to put easy, general questions at the very beginning of a survey?

options.A: To trick the participant into answering difficult items quickly
options.B: To ensure the statistical software can read the demographic data
options.C: To shorten the total amount of time needed for data collection
options.D: To help the participant feel comfortable and build trust

explanation: Starting with gentle, straightforward questions eases anxiety and encourages people to complete the rest of the questionnaire. Brilliant thinking!

question: When we talk about extracellular fluid (ECF) outside our cells, what are its two main parts?

options.A: Intracellular fluid and plasma
options.B: Cerebrospinal fluid and synovial fluid
options.C: Intracellular fluid and interstitial fluid
options.D: Intravascular fluid and interstitial fluid

explanation: Nice try! ECF is basically the fluid inside your blood vessels (plasma) plus the fluid resting right between your tissues (interstitial fluid). You're mastering body fluids step by step!

question: A nurse wants to assess how community members handle their household drinking water. Which method is most appropriate?

options.A: Calculating annual hospital mortality statistics
options.B: Analyzing international disease journals
options.C: Reading national population census booklets
options.D: Direct observation of water storage practices

explanation: Direct observation allows the nurse to see actual daily behaviors regarding water handling rather than relying on reported answers. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a feature of an Addisonian crisis?

options.A: Vascular collapse and shock
options.B: Profound low blood pressure
options.C: Severe high blood pressure
options.D: Severe vomiting and pain

explanation: An Addisonian crisis causes a dangerous crash in blood pressure (hypotension), not high blood pressure.

question: Why do we say communication is a clinical intervention, just like giving medicine?

options.A: It requires a written doctor's prescription before it can occur.
options.B: It carries the exact same legal risks as giving an intravenous drug.
options.C: It directly influences patient health outcomes and healing environments.
options.D: It is recorded on the medication administration record every shift.

explanation: You got it! Just like a tablet or injection, the words you use can genuinely help a patient heal and feel better.

question: Which finding is most commonly auscultated in the lungs of a patient experiencing fluid overload?

options.A: High-pitched whistling wheezes
options.B: Absent breath sounds on the left
options.C: A loud friction rub over the trachea
options.D: Fine crackles at the lung bases

explanation: Fluid backing up into the tiny air sacs of the lungs creates a crackling sound when air pops them open during inhalation. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T3#GNS311_U2_T3_h5)

question: A pregnant teenager attends an antenatal clinic and exhibits signs she is at risk of being forced into early marriage. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Ignore the situation because family matters are private
options.B: Call local police immediately while she is still in the exam room
options.C: Lecture her parents harshly in front of the other waiting patients
options.D: Provide a safe, confidential space to assess her safety and offer support

explanation: Creating a confidential environment allows the nurse to gauge immediate danger and connect the patient with protective services safely. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h6)

question: Why do we generally avoid giving live vaccines to pregnant women?

options.A: Live vaccines deactivate automatically in pregnant bloodstreams
options.B: Hormonal changes turn live viruses into strong bacteria
options.C: Pregnant women always develop permanent immunity instantly
options.D: There is a theoretical risk of harming the developing fetus

explanation: Live vaccines contain weakened germs that might pose risks during pregnancy, so we prefer using safe, inactivated options instead.

question: Which statement best demonstrates empathy toward a client struggling with a new diagnosis?

options.A: You just need to follow your medication list every single day.
options.B: It must be really hard to adjust to these new lifestyle changes.
options.C: Why did you wait so long to see a doctor about your symptoms?
options.D: Everyone gets this disease eventually, so do not worry too much.

explanation: Acknowledging the client's emotional struggle shows empathy by validating their personal experience with the illness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h4)

question: What is the main reason a medication dropper should never touch the patient's skin or eyelashes?

options.A: To prevent contaminating the entire medication bottle with germs
options.B: To stop the liquid from flowing out too fast
options.C: To keep the glass tip from breaking off inside the canal
options.D: To avoid causing a sudden sharp pain for the patient

explanation: Touching the eye or ear transfers bacteria to the dropper tip, which then contaminates the remaining liquid inside the bottle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which stage of labour has the highest risk for heavy bleeding (postpartum hemorrhage)?

options.A: Latent phase
options.B: Second stage
options.C: Fourth stage
options.D: First stage

explanation: The fourth stage is the immediate hour or two after delivery. We monitor mums extra closely here because the uterus needs to clamp down firmly to stop bleeding.

question: What is an important way community health nurses can help prevent FGM?

options.A: Performing mild forms of FGM under hygienic conditions
options.B: Issuing legal certificates permitting traditional circumcisers
options.C: Subsidizing the cost of traditional ceremonies
options.D: Educating local communities about the health risks of FGM

explanation: Spot on! Community health nurses play a huge role in prevention by raising awareness and teaching families about the dangers of FGM. Brilliant work today!

question: During the extension movement, what part of the baby's face sweeps out of the vagina first?

options.A: The bridge of the nose
options.B: The forehead and brows
options.C: The chin and mouth
options.D: The parietal eminences

explanation: You got it! As the head pivots up, the chin, mouth, and nose peek out first from under the perineum.

question: Why must a nurse know both the generic and brand names of a medication?

options.A: To ensure the hospital charges the patient the highest possible fee
options.B: To prevent medication errors during charting and prescription checks
options.C: To help patients manufacture their own medicines at home safely
options.D: To comply with legal rules requiring nurses to write prescriptions

explanation: Knowing both names protects your patient. If a doctor writes a brand name and the chart has the generic, you'll instantly spot it and prevent accidental double-dosing!

question: Why do mothers who have given birth before (multiparous women) often feel stronger afterpains than first-time mothers?

options.A: Their perineal wounds are always surgically larger
options.B: They are more sensitive to standard doses of analgesics
options.C: They produce significantly less lochia than primiparous mothers
options.D: Their uterine muscles lose tone and contract intermittently with greater force

explanation: Because her uterus has worked before, it doesn't stay clamped down all at once. Instead, it relaxes and contracts rhythmically, leading to stronger cramps as it gets back into shape.

question: What usually happens if a clinic or hospital runs without clear objectives?

options.A: Operational costs drop significantly across all departments.
options.B: Staff morale improves because there is less pressure.
options.C: Patient satisfaction automatically reaches maximum levels.
options.D: Resources are wasted and priorities become unclear.

explanation: Without a clear roadmap, everyone ends up pulling in different directions, leading to wasted time and resources. Clear goals keep the team aligned!

question: How would you best describe Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)?

options.A: A degenerative muscular disease
options.B: A lifelong neurodevelopmental condition
options.C: A preventable infectious illness
options.D: A temporary childhood behavioral phase

explanation: You've got this! Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition, meaning it stays with a person throughout their entire life. It's just a different way of experiencing the world.

question: A nurse is teaching range-of-motion exercises to a patient recovering from a stroke. Which level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Rehabilitation and preventing further disability from an established disease fall under tertiary prevention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h3)

question: Why is it helpful for nurses to know a hormone's chemical structure?

options.A: It shows whether the hormone is made of white blood cells
options.B: It predicts how they travel in blood and interact with target cells
options.C: It dictates the exact caloric value of the hormone in the diet
options.D: It determines the exact time of day the gland will secrete them

explanation: Knowing whether a hormone is water-soluble or fat-soluble helps us understand how it moves through the blood and finds its target. Clinical pharmacology becomes much easier when you master this basics!

question: Why do lymph nodes often swell up and feel tender when you have an infection?

options.A: White blood cells multiply rapidly inside the node to fight pathogens
options.B: Blood flow to the node temporarily stops completely
options.C: Trapped fluid stretches the outer capsule of the node permanently
options.D: Red blood cells leak out of nearby capillaries into the node

explanation: When germs arrive, your white blood cells throw a massive defense party inside the node, multiplying quickly to fight off the infection. That crowding is what causes the swelling and tenderness!

question: What common blood collection mistake can make a patient's potassium level look falsely high on a lab report?

options.A: Hemolysis of the blood sample
options.B: Using a small gauge needle for a deep vein
options.C: Leaving the tourniquet on for too short a time
options.D: Storing the sample inside a warm incubator

explanation: Spot on! If red blood cells break open (hemolyze) during a rough blood draw, they spill their inner potassium into the sample, giving a fake high reading.

question: What is the main purpose of secondary prevention, like routine screenings?

options.A: Stopping environmental toxins from entering the local community
options.B: Preventing healthy individuals from ever encountering risk factors
options.C: Restoring full physical strength after cancer treatment finishes
options.D: Detecting disease early when it is easiest and most successful to treat

explanation: Secondary prevention is all about catching things early through screening so you can tackle them before they grow into a bigger problem.

question: Which type of injury happens at the exact moment a physical blow or crash occurs?

options.A: Metabolic injury
options.B: Primary injury
options.C: Tertiary injury
options.D: Secondary injury

explanation: That's correct! The primary injury is the immediate damage that happens right at the time of impact, like torn tissue or bruising.

question: When doing a community assessment, what does 'resource mapping' actually involve?

options.A: Counting how many patients die in the regional hospital
options.B: Listing roads that need paving by the federal government
options.C: Identifying local strengths, active groups, and facilities
options.D: Calculating the exact profit of local medicine shops

explanation: Resource mapping is like drawing a treasure map of your community's strengths—finding local groups, clinics, and assets that can help improve health.

question: What is the main difference between blood plasma and serum?

options.A: Plasma is found outside blood vessels while serum is found inside
options.B: Plasma contains red blood cells while serum contains only white blood cells
options.C: Serum lacks clotting proteins like fibrinogen because it has already clotted
options.D: Serum has a much higher water content than plasma

explanation: Spot on! Think of serum as plasma that has finished doing its clotting job; the clotting proteins (like fibrinogen) get used up during the clot, leaving serum behind.

question: Why do nurses always warn patients with bleeding problems to stay away from everyday painkillers like ibuprofen?

options.A: NSAIDs increase blood pressure to dangerous levels and trigger acute strokes
options.B: NSAIDs instantly destroy all stored vitamin K reserves located inside the liver
options.C: NSAIDs negatively interfere with normal platelet aggregation and increase bleeding risks
options.D: NSAIDs cause the kidneys to stop producing red blood cells permanently

explanation: Medications like ibuprofen and aspirin get in the way of platelets sticking together, making it much harder for your body to stop any bleeding.

question: Why are older adults more likely to experience adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Their bodies absorb medications much faster than younger people
options.B: Older skin cannot absorb pills properly
options.C: They always refuse to take prescribed doses
options.D: Age-related slowdown in kidney and liver function

explanation: As we age, our kidneys and liver process drugs more slowly. This means medications stay in the body longer and can build up to toxic levels.

question: What is the main goal of the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: To restrict patient access to common over-the-counter drugs
options.B: To make safe and effective medicines affordable and available
options.C: To eliminate the need for international pharmaceutical trade
options.D: To promote expensive brand-name pharmaceuticals in hospitals

explanation: You got this! The core idea is simple: making sure everyday life-saving medicines remain cheap enough and within reach for everyone who needs them.

question: A patient sits crying silently in bed after receiving a terminal diagnosis. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Turn on the television to distract them from sadness
options.B: Remind them that modern medicine is very advanced
options.C: Leave the room immediately to give them privacy
options.D: Sit quietly beside the patient and offer a reassuring touch

explanation: Offering presence and gentle touch shows support and lets the patient know they are not alone in their grief. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h6)

question: Why does flying at high altitudes put patients at risk for low oxygen levels (hypoxia)?

options.A: The barometric pressure drops, reducing available oxygen levels
options.B: Cold cabin temperatures destroy red blood cells
options.C: The aircraft engines consume all the oxygen in the cabin
options.D: Patients stop breathing naturally due to engine noise

explanation: You got it! As you go higher up, atmospheric pressure drops, making it harder for oxygen to pass into the lungs. That's why cabin oxygen monitoring is so crucial.

question: Why is respecting local culture vital during a community health campaign?

options.A: It prevents nurses from learning any new languages
options.B: It ensures that western medicine is completely ignored
options.C: It builds trust and encourages people to accept the health message
options.D: It allows the nurse to change the local religious practices

explanation: When health workers honor local customs and beliefs, community members feel respected and are much more likely to cooperate. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is checking bowel movements extra important for patients taking opioid pain medications for a fracture?

options.A: Pain medications speed up digestion too much and cause diarrhea.
options.B: Opioids destroy beneficial bacteria living inside the large intestine.
options.C: Opioids frequently cause significant and uncomfortable constipation.
options.D: Pain medications prevent the body from absorbing dietary calcium.

explanation: Opioids slow down the gut big time. Anticipating and preventing constipation is a huge part of keeping patients comfortable during recovery.

question: In Nigeria, what is the leading cause of vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Severe bacterial kidney disease
options.C: Untreated urinary tract infections
options.D: Prolonged obstructed labour

explanation: Great job! When labour is stuck, the baby's head presses hard against the pelvis, cutting off blood supply and causing tissue to break down. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h2)

question: Why are small, frequent meals recommended for patients recovering from acute pancreatitis?

options.A: They prevent the stomach from absorbing too much plain water
options.B: They guarantee rapid weight gain during hospital recovery
options.C: They reduce the digestive workload on the pancreas at any one time
options.D: They completely eliminate the need to monitor fat gram counts

explanation: Spot on! Smaller portions mean less digestive stress for an already overworked, inflamed pancreas.

question: What is the primary purpose of the teach-back method in health education?

options.A: To evaluate the environmental noise levels in a clinic room
options.B: To document medical history in a formal hospital chart
options.C: To check if the client understands the instructions by having them repeat them
options.D: To test the nurse's ability to lecture a large community group

explanation: Teach-back allows nurses to verify comprehension by asking clients to explain back what was taught in their own words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h8)

question: When would the Ministry of Health use syndromic surveillance?

options.A: When they want to check the exact financial budget of a rural hospital
options.B: When they need the absolute fastest warning about a potential outbreak based on symptoms
options.C: When laboratory tests are cheap and results are ready within minutes
options.D: When they need a complete census of all chronic illnesses

explanation: Syndromic surveillance watches out for symptom groups (like sudden fever and rashes) even before lab results come back, giving us a super-fast early alarm!

question: What should meeting minutes mainly focus on writing down?

options.A: Personal opinions of staff members about hospital leadership
options.B: Decisions made, assigned tasks, and agreed deadlines
options.C: Detailed medical histories of individual patients
options.D: Verbatim transcripts of every joke told in the room

explanation: Minutes capture concrete outcomes and action items, not a word-for-word playback of the whole conversation.

question: Why might the standard 0-to-10 numeric pain scale be tricky to use for an adult with severe dementia?

options.A: Numeric scales only work for surgical wounds
options.B: Patients with dementia lose the ability to speak at all
options.C: They will always just say ten no matter what
options.D: They may struggle to connect a number to how they feel

explanation: Well reasoned! Numbers are abstract concepts. For patients with cognitive changes, we often need to rely on facial expression charts or physical behavior cues instead.

question: What is the most important factor an educator must check before selecting a teaching aid?

options.A: Whether it has bright, attractive colors
options.B: Whether it matches the lesson objectives
options.C: If it is the most expensive brand available
options.D: If it requires electricity to function

explanation: No matter how advanced a material is, it fails its educational purpose if it does not help achieve the specific learning goals of the class. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h4)

question: Why does a community nurse look at the whole household instead of just one sick person?

options.A: Diseases always hit every family member at the exact same second
options.B: National insurance only pays for whole households
options.C: Hospital rules ban treating single patients alone
options.D: Family members share the same living conditions, risks, and environment

explanation: Brilliant! Since family members eat from the same pot and live under the same roof, a health risk or crisis usually affects everyone in the home.

question: What major event marks the exact beginning of the third stage of labour?

options.A: Complete dilation of the cervix
options.B: Delivery of the infant
options.C: Expulsion of the mucous plug
options.D: Rupture of the amniotic membranes

explanation: Great thinking! The moment the baby is safely out, the third stage kicks off—and it wraps up once the placenta is delivered too.

question: When should you as a nurse hold off on bladder irrigation unless the doctor specifically says it's okay?

options.A: When there is suspected trauma to the urinary tract
options.B: When urine output drops slightly over a two-hour window
options.C: When cloudy urine appears in the clear drainage tubing
options.D: When the patient reports mild burning around the meatus

explanation: Safety first! If the urinary tract is injured, pushing fluid in can force bacteria and fluid straight out into the pelvic tissue through the tear.

question: Where do water-soluble peptide hormones usually find their target cell receptors?

options.A: On the outer surface of the target cell membrane
options.B: Attached to the outer wall of blood capillaries
options.C: Deep inside the nucleus of the target cell
options.D: Floating freely within the cytoplasm of the cell

explanation: Since water-soluble hormones can't cross the fatty cell membrane barrier, they have to knock on the front door by binding to receptors on the outside surface of the cell.

question: Why do food manufacturers sometimes use multiple different names for sugar on a single ingredient list?

options.A: To divide the total amount so individual sugars appear further down the weight-based ingredient list
options.B: To make the product taste better by combining artificial and natural sweeteners together
options.C: To prevent the food from spoiling too quickly on supermarket shelves
options.D: To comply with strict international laws requiring chemical names for every single food item

explanation: It's a clever marketing trick! By splitting sugar into three or four different names, manufacturers can scatter them down the list so the product looks healthier than it really is.

question: A patient walks barefoot on a damp beach where stray dogs pass by, and later presents with itchy, winding red tracks on their foot. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Guinea worm infection
options.B: Furunculoid myiasis
options.C: Cutaneous larva migrans
options.D: Acute malaria

explanation: Walking barefoot on soil contaminated with animal hookworm larvae leads right to skin penetration and those classic creeping eruption tracks.

question: Which group of medications is usually given first to stop a long-lasting seizure?

options.A: Diuretics
options.B: Opioid analgesics
options.C: Beta-blockers
options.D: Benzodiazepines

explanation: Correct! Fast-acting benzodiazepines are the go-to emergency drugs to calm down runaway brain activity quickly.

question: Why shouldn't you try to push a protruding bone back under the skin during emergency care?

options.A: It can damage surrounding blood vessels and nerves and introduce deep infection.
options.B: It causes immediate paralysis of the entire central nervous system.
options.C: It makes it impossible for the doctor to take a clear X-ray later.
options.D: It automatically guarantees that the bone will never heal properly.

explanation: Pushing it back in can accidentally slice major blood vessels or nerves, and drag surface germs deep inside the sterile bone. Always leave bone repositioning to the medical team!

question: What do we call the chemical messengers that cross the synaptic cleft?

options.A: Antibodies
options.B: Neurotransmitters
options.C: Electrolytes
options.D: Plasma proteins

explanation: Neurotransmitters are the chemical bridge-builders that help a message jump across the tiny gap (synapse) from one neuron to the next.

question: In Superior Mesenteric Artery syndrome, what actually squeezes or traps the duodenum?

options.A: Compression of the bowel between the aorta and a major artery
options.B: A large benign tumor growing inside the intestinal lining
options.C: Severe twisting of the small intestine around its own blood supply
options.D: Scar tissue buildup following multiple abdominal surgeries

explanation: That's correct! When protective fat is lost, the superior mesenteric artery can press down and trap part of the duodenum right against the big aorta.

question: What core toxicological principle states that virtually any substance can act as a poison if the quantity is large enough?

options.A: All chemicals are inherently lethal
options.B: The route determines toxicity
options.C: Metabolism prevents all toxicity
options.D: The dose makes the poison

explanation: Toxicology teaches that safety and toxicity depend on the amount of exposure, meaning harmless substances can become dangerous in excessive quantities. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h1)

question: What is the main goal of managing a healthcare facility's infrastructure?

options.A: Reducing the total number of clinical staff employed in the hospital
options.B: Minimizing the purchase of new medical and diagnostic equipment
options.C: Ensuring physical assets support patient safety and staff productivity
options.D: Maximizing the financial profit of the facility above all else

explanation: Think of infrastructure management as making sure the building and equipment help nurses care for patients safely and smoothly without unnecessary stress!

question: Why is it crucial to check vital signs before giving a heart medication?

options.A: To determine if the patient has eaten a heavy meal recently
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of the medication dose
options.C: To verify the correct room number of the hospitalized patient
options.D: To ensure the patient's blood pressure or pulse is not already too low

explanation: Cardiovascular drugs naturally lower BP or heart rate. If your patient's vitals are already crashing, giving the drug could cause dangerous shock!

question: A patient has severe burns on their chest. Why does putting medicated cream here put them at risk for drug overload?

options.A: Burns block all local blood flow, causing the drug to pool dangerously under the skin.
options.B: Burned skin traps the medication and forces it to travel directly to the liver.
options.C: The protective stratum corneum is damaged, allowing rapid and excessive drug entry into the bloodstream.
options.D: Damaged skin cells chemically react with the cream to create new toxins.

explanation: You're learning fast! When burns or wounds damage the skin's outer guard layer, too much medicine can rush into the bloodstream all at once.

question: Which hormones keep milk production on hold during pregnancy?

options.A: Thyroxine and adrenaline
options.B: Prolactin and oxytocin
options.C: Estrogen and progesterone
options.D: Insulin and cortisol

explanation: Well done! High levels of these pregnancy hormones help the breasts grow, but they block actual milk flow until the baby is born.

question: What is the main advantage of a self-retaining retractor like the Weitlaner?

options.A: It locks open automatically, freeing up assistant hands
options.B: It has a built-in light source to illuminate deep wounds
options.C: It does not require any sterilization between cases
options.D: It can also be used as a cutting instrument for bone

explanation: Self-retaining retractors use a ratchet lock to stay open on their own, reducing fatigue for the surgical team. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is a recommended strategy when communicating with an elderly client who has mild hearing loss?

options.A: Direct all your questions to their young family members
options.B: Write everything down and refuse to speak out loud
options.C: Shout at the top of your lungs from across the room
options.D: Speak clearly in a normal tone without shouting

explanation: Shouting distorts sound and can sound aggressive. Speaking clearly at a moderate pitch and facing the client works best for mild hearing loss. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of involving local residents in data collection?

options.A: It allows nurses to stay inside the office all day long
options.B: It builds local ownership and trust in health programs
options.C: It forces community members to pay taxes to the clinic
options.D: It removes the need for professional nursing training

explanation: When residents participate in the diagnostic process, they value the resulting health interventions and support them willingly. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which key immune cells are primarily attacked and destroyed by HIV?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Red blood cells
options.C: CD4+ T-lymphocytes
options.D: Platelets

explanation: Correct! HIV specifically targets CD4+ T-cells, using them to make copies of itself and gradually weakening the body's immune defense.
