question: What is an important way nurses can guide patients and visitors regarding ward waste?

options.A: Revising the hospital's annual financial budget
options.B: Teaching them how to operate surgical autoclaves
options.C: Explaining the correct use of color-coded waste bins
options.D: Training them to administer intravenous injections

explanation: Visitors often toss things into the nearest bin. Taking a second to guide them helps keep our color-coded waste streams pure!

question: At what age is primary amenorrhoea typically considered if a young girl has normal breast and pubic hair development but no period yet?

options.A: 18 years
options.B: 11 years
options.C: 15 years
options.D: 21 years

explanation: We look out for primary amenorrhoea if a girl reaches age 15 without starting her period, even though her other puberty signs are normal.

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care for a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: Taking over all daily tasks completely
options.B: Focusing solely on the medical diagnosis
options.C: Promoting independence, dignity, and safety
options.D: Confining the patient to strict bed rest

explanation: Nursing care aims to support the person's remaining abilities while keeping them safe and preserving their personal dignity. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h1)

question: What is a very common cause of accidental needle-stick injuries among nurses?

options.A: Disinfecting rubber seals on vials
options.B: Manually recapping used needles
options.C: Using single-dose medication vials
options.D: Dropping plastic syringe barrels

explanation: Try to avoid recapping used needles whenever possible! Missing the cap is the easiest way to accidentally poke your own finger.

question: What is a major safety concern when giving sleeping pills (sedative-hypnotics) to older adults?

options.A: Severe respiratory alkalosis
options.B: Hypertensive crisis
options.C: Permanent hearing loss
options.D: Increased risk of falls

explanation: Sleeping pills can cause daytime drowsiness and dizziness, making older adults unsteady on their feet and putting them at a high risk for accidental falls.

question: What is the primary goal of prescribing symptomatic medications in degenerative conditions?

options.A: To improve patient comfort and daily functioning
options.B: To stop all future cell death in the brain
options.C: To completely cure the underlying chronic illness
options.D: To permanently reverse any genetic mutations

explanation: You nailed it! When a disease can't be cured yet, our nursing focus shifts to easing symptoms so the patient can stay comfortable and independent for as long as possible.

question: Which option best describes true informed consent in clinical research?

options.A: An agreement signed by the hospital manager on behalf of the patients
options.B: A verbal promise made by the researcher that no complications will occur
options.C: An ongoing, voluntary dialogue ensuring participants understand risks and rights
options.D: A quick signature obtained by a doctor right before a surgical procedure

explanation: Informed consent isn't just a one-time signature. It's a continuous conversation making sure the participant is fully aware and knows they can walk away anytime. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h4)

question: How does the progestin in injectable contraceptives mainly stop sperm from reaching an egg?

options.A: By thickening cervical mucus to create a barrier
options.B: By neutralizing the natural acid inside the vagina
options.C: By dissolving sperm cells on contact
options.D: By causing the fallopian tubes to tie themselves

explanation: Think of it like a security guard: the hormone makes the cervical mucus thick and sticky so sperm can't swim up into the womb!

question: What causes extra or missing chromosomes, like in Down syndrome?

options.A: Eating too much sugar over the years
options.B: Rapid multiplication of red blood cells during an infection
options.C: A physical injury to the skin in childhood
options.D: Chromosomes failing to separate properly during cell division

explanation: When chromosomes don't pull apart neatly during cell division, the resulting cells can end up with an extra or missing chromosome. You've got this!

question: A patient says they feel constantly exhausted, lack energy for simple chores, and sleep does not help at all. How should you, as the nurse, categorize this?

options.A: As normal tiredness
options.B: As circadian misalignment
options.C: As acute somnolence
options.D: As clinical fatigue

explanation: Well done! When sleep doesn't touch the exhaustion and it starts disrupting daily life, we call it clinical fatigue rather than regular tiredness.

question: How high should an infant's bottom be from the mattress in Gallows traction?

options.A: Lifted just barely so a hand can slide underneath
options.B: Raised at least twelve inches high
options.C: Tilted completely sideways
options.D: Pressed firmly against the mattress

explanation: Just a tiny lift is the magic trick! It uses the baby's own upper body weight to create the counter-pulling force.

question: What tends to happen to the basal metabolic rate during long periods of severe calorie restriction?

options.A: It fluctuates every single hour
options.B: It slows down to conserve energy
options.C: It stops functioning completely
options.D: It increases to burn extra glucose

explanation: Correct! Your body is smart—when it senses very low food intake, it slows down its metabolism to save energy, which can make further weight loss slower.

question: What is the main focus of a servant leader in nursing?

options.A: Prioritizing the growth and well-being of the healthcare team
options.B: Strictly punishing staff who make minor documentation errors
options.C: Avoiding all interaction with junior nursing personnel
options.D: Maintaining absolute control over all hospital financial budgets

explanation: A servant leader puts the team first. By making sure nurses are supported and well-cared for, patient care naturally becomes top-notch!

question: What is the very first thing you must check before helping someone who has collapsed?

options.A: Scene safety
options.B: Blood pressure
options.C: The patient's pulse
options.D: Pupil reaction

explanation: Safety first! Always check that the environment is safe for you before rushing in to help. We need you safe too!

question: Which core principle of health advocacy is all about fair distribution of health resources?

options.A: Patient autonomy
options.B: Clinical competence
options.C: Strict confidentiality
options.D: Social justice

explanation: Spot on! Social justice is about making sure health resources actually reach the people who need them most, keeping things fair and equal.

question: What is the very first test usually done to check for male factor infertility?

options.A: Testicular biopsy
options.B: Scrotal ultrasound
options.C: Hormone blood panel
options.D: Semen analysis

explanation: A semen analysis is the simplest and most helpful first step to check sperm count, movement, and shape. You've got this!

question: A child is rushed to the ward with severe, complicated malaria. What is the best first step regarding their medications?

options.A: Refuse treatment until the family pays cash for the full prescription
options.B: Wait for hospital accountants to review the family's bank statements
options.C: Send the parents out to buy drugs from a commercial chemist across the street
options.D: Provide necessary emergency anti-malarials immediately under the exemption policy

explanation: Spot on! Severe pediatric emergencies qualify for immediate medication access to save the child's life without delay.

question: Which common pregnancy complication is closely linked to widespread placental infarctions (tissue death)?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Preeclampsia
options.C: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: High blood pressure disorders like preeclampsia narrow the tiny blood vessels in the placenta, cutting off proper blood flow and causing small areas of tissue to die. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h5)

question: A patient scheduled for a procedure with mild sedation asks for a glass of water an hour beforehand. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Explain that fasting guidelines must be followed to prevent aspiration during sedation.
options.B: Ignore the question because fluid intake does not affect anesthesia safety.
options.C: Tell the patient to drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated before the test.
options.D: Allow the patient to drink a small cup of water since it is just a liquid.

explanation: Fasting (NPO) keeps the stomach empty so the patient doesn't accidentally choke or inhale stomach contents while sedated. Safety first!

question: What is a fixed cost in a healthcare unit?

options.A: The variable wages paid to casual registry nurses
options.B: A cost that changes daily based on medication usage
options.C: An expense that stays the same regardless of patient numbers
options.D: An emergency fund used only for unexpected equipment breakdowns

explanation: Fixed costs stay stable month after month, no matter if your ward is overflowing with patients or half-empty!

question: Why can taking regular doses of NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) lead to stomach ulcers?

options.A: They block protective chemicals (prostaglandins) that help build stomach mucus
options.B: They paralyze the smooth muscles responsible for stomach movement
options.C: They directly increase the total amount of acid in your stomach
options.D: They force the lower esophageal sphincter to stay wide open all day

explanation: NSAIDs block helpful prostaglandins, which strips away your stomach's natural mucus and bicarbonate armor, leaving the tissue vulnerable to acid damage.

question: How do assisted living facilities differ from traditional nursing homes?

options.A: Assisted living requires continuous 24-hour physician supervision.
options.B: Nursing homes provide much less medical oversight than assisted living.
options.C: Nursing homes only admit individuals who are completely independent.
options.D: Assisted living focuses more on a home-like setting and independence.

explanation: While nursing homes offer heavy, continuous medical and nursing care, assisted living emphasizes residential comfort and autonomy with lesser medical intervention. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h1)

question: What actually happens when there is 'sampling bias' in research?

options.A: An error caused by using a broken weighing scale in the clinic
options.B: The refusal of patients to answer personal questions in a survey
options.C: A systematic flaw that favors certain individuals over others in selection
options.D: The natural mathematical difference between a sample and a population

explanation: Spot on! Sampling bias means your selection method accidentally gives some people a better chance of being picked than others, skewing your results.

question: What is the purpose of drawing an epidemic curve during an investigation?

options.A: To measure the physical distance between infected houses
options.B: To test the purity of local water supplies in a lab
options.C: To visualize how the infection spread over time
options.D: To calculate the total budget spent on patient drugs

explanation: An epidemic curve is a graph that shows the onset of cases over time, helping investigators understand the outbreak's pattern. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: Why does a nurse need to ask when a patient's symptoms first started?

options.A: Chronic symptoms never require medical treatment
options.B: Rapid onset points to acute problems, while slow onset suggests chronic imbalances
options.C: Insurance companies require exact dates before approving lab tests
options.D: It helps the patient remember to take their medication on time

explanation: Exactly! The timeline helps you figure out if this is a sudden emergency or a long-standing, slow-burning hormonal issue.

question: How do daily routines and familiar activities help a patient with dementia during recovery?

options.A: They completely reverse brain cell death caused by Alzheimer's disease
options.B: They cure chronic sleep apnea permanently
options.C: They eliminate the need for any physical therapy exercises
options.D: They reduce confusion and help the patient feel secure enough to participate

explanation: Exactly right! Predictable routines calm anxiety and make confused patients feel safe enough to cooperate with care.

question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during intrapartum care?

options.A: To test the mother's blood sugar levels
options.B: To register the baby's name after birth
options.C: To calculate the total cost of hospital delivery
options.D: To monitor the progress of labor and detect problems early

explanation: The partograph is a visual tool used by nurses and midwives to track labor progress and maternal-fetal well-being. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h4)

question: A pregnant woman in a village clinic avoids meat and fish because elders said it causes difficult labor. What is the main health risk here?

options.A: Severe dehydration from high sodium intake
options.B: Maternal anemia and poor fetal development
options.C: Excessive weight gain during the first trimester
options.D: Sudden elevation of blood glucose levels

explanation: Skipping protein and iron during pregnancy denies both mother and baby essential building blocks, which can lead to anemia and slow growth.

question: What is the main job of enzymes in our metabolism?

options.A: They carry oxygen from the lungs to the body tissues.
options.B: They act as the main structural material for skin cells.
options.C: They store energy as fat for future survival needs.
options.D: They speed up chemical reactions as biological catalysts.

explanation: Think of enzymes as tiny biological helpers that speed up chemical reactions in the body without getting used up themselves.

question: What do the letters in the SBAR handover tool stand for?

options.A: System, Bedside, Analysis, Report
options.B: Symptoms, Breathing, Airway, Respiration
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Safety, Balance, Assessment, Recovery

explanation: You nailed it! SBAR is your best friend for giving quick, structured, and clear patient updates to other healthcare workers.

question: In which part of the abdomen is the main portion of the stomach located?

options.A: Lower left quadrant
options.B: Upper left quadrant
options.C: Upper right quadrant
options.D: Lower right quadrant

explanation: Think of the abdomen in four quarters. The stomach rests comfortably right up in the upper left section, just below your diaphragm.

question: Which of the following is a known risk of poorly managed government price controls?

options.A: Supermarkets will automatically lower prices on all luxury items
options.B: Agricultural land will turn into high-yield forest reserves
options.C: Farmers may stop growing crops if prices do not cover production costs
options.D: Consumers will completely stop purchasing staple foods

explanation: If price caps are set too low, farmers lose money and reduce future production, causing scarcity. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h5)

question: What is the term for high blood pressure that has no single identifiable medical cause?

options.A: Primary hypertension
options.B: Malignant hypertension
options.C: Gestational hypertension
options.D: Secondary hypertension

explanation: Primary or essential hypertension makes up the vast majority of cases and develops gradually from lifestyle and genetic factors. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h2)

question: What is the best nursing approach for a patient feeling extremely fatigued from acute hepatitis?

options.A: Balancing activity with planned rest periods to conserve energy
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent swelling in the abdomen
options.C: Keeping the patient on strict bed rest with no movement allowed
options.D: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to stimulate metabolism

explanation: Smart nursing care! Pacing out activities with plenty of rest helps the patient's body heal without letting them get stiff or weak from being stuck in bed all day.

question: A patient with type 1 diabetes lives somewhere without reliable electricity and asks how to keep their insulin cool. What is a helpful, practical suggestion?

options.A: Use a clay pot evaporative cooler system to store the insulin safely
options.B: Keep the insulin bottle in direct sunlight to keep it warm and dry
options.C: Store the insulin inside the family cooking pot near the fireplace
options.D: Leave the insulin exposed on the open windowsill during the night

explanation: Brilliant! A clay pot cooler (pot-in-pot evaporative cooling) is a fantastic, traditional way to lower storage temperatures without needing a fridge or electricity.

question: Why do nurses need to check a patient's other medications when starting an antiparasitic drug that goes through the liver?

options.A: Liver enzymes completely neutralize the therapeutic effect of all parasites
options.B: Patients with liver issues cannot absorb any form of topical cream
options.C: Many antiparasitic drugs are metabolized by liver enzymes, altering blood levels
options.D: Hepatic enzymes prevent gastrointestinal side effects entirely

explanation: The liver handles many of these drugs. If another medicine speeds up or slows down those liver enzymes, it can accidentally cause drug toxicity or make the treatment fail.

question: What is the main reason we use stitches to close a simple skin cut?

options.A: To reduce healing time and minimize scarring
options.B: To stop deep muscle spasms near the injury site
options.C: To permanently eliminate all risk of bacterial infection
options.D: To replace the need for a tetanus toxoid booster

explanation: You've got this! Bringing the skin edges neatly together helps the cut heal much faster and keeps the scar as small as possible. Great job!

question: A nurse wants to address high salt intake in a local market. What should be the very first step?

options.A: Engage market vendors in a discussion about how they view salt use in local foods
options.B: Ban the sale of heavily salted processed snacks within the market stalls
options.C: Organize a mandatory lecture hall seminar for all registered market traders
options.D: Distribute brightly coloured pamphlets detailing the dangers of hypertension

explanation: Brilliant! True nursing care starts with listening. Always involve the community and understand their perspective before trying to change their habits.

question: Which social factor is consistently proven to help young girls delay marriage and early childbearing?

options.A: Traditional community ceremonies
options.B: Living in an urban city center
options.C: Access to formal education
options.D: Employment in the agricultural sector

explanation: Education is a powerful tool! When girls stay in school, they gain knowledge, open up better life opportunities, and naturally delay marriage and childbearing.

question: What is the big worry with secondary brain injuries after a sudden head trauma or stroke?

options.A: Cellular damage continues to unfold over hours and days after the initial insult.
options.B: All injured neurons instantly recover full electrical function within minutes.
options.C: Blood pressure drops to zero throughout the entire systemic circulation.
options.D: The immune system completely stops responding to any external pathogens.

explanation: Even after the primary event stops, things like swelling and chemical stress keep destroying tissue over the next few hours or days.

question: What is the medical name for nearsightedness?

options.A: Hyperopia
options.B: Myopia
options.C: Presbyopia
options.D: Astigmatism

explanation: Myopia means you can see things close up clearly, but far-away objects look blurry because light focuses just short of the retina.

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for triggering the milk 'let-down' reflex when breastfeeding?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Wonderful! Oxytocin makes tiny muscles around the milk glands squeeze, pushing the milk forward for the baby. It's also the hormone of love and bonding!

question: What crucial nursing check must be done before giving food or water to a stroke patient who might have trouble swallowing?

options.A: A check for homonymous hemianopsia
options.B: A measurement of 24-hour urine output
options.C: A formal bedside swallow screen
options.D: A complete neurological Glasgow Coma Scale score

explanation: Correct! Swallowing difficulties (dysphagia) can easily lead to aspiration pneumonia. A bedside swallow screen keeps the patient safe before any oral intake.

question: Why is inhaling a chemical often more dangerous than getting it on your skin?

options.A: Rapid absorption into the bloodstream through the lungs
options.B: Localized swelling of the eye tissues
options.C: Delayed stomach ulceration and internal bleeding
options.D: Immediate burning of the outer skin layers

explanation: Think of the lungs as a massive highway into the body! Inhaled substances quickly cross into the tiny blood vessels (capillaries) in the lungs and travel straight to vital organs.

question: What is the main health risk of breathing in silica or asbestos dust over a long time?

options.A: Progressive lung scarring and breathing damage
options.B: Severe joint pain in the fingers
options.C: Rapid hair loss and skin discoloration
options.D: Sudden hearing loss in both ears

explanation: Inhaling mineral dust causes chronic irritation and permanent scarring inside the lungs, making it much harder to breathe over time.

question: A nurse makes a medication calculation error because orientation on the new infusion pump was rushed. What is the root cause?

options.A: Lack of knowledge or training
options.B: Willful defiance of hospital policy
options.C: An intentional desire to cause harm
options.D: Personal substance abuse issues

explanation: When a nurse makes a mistake due to poor orientation, the primary issue is a lack of proper training. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h4)

question: Where should used injection needles and sharp blades be discarded?

options.A: Puncture-proof sharps containers
options.B: Red infectious linen laundry bags
options.C: Open cardboard boxes near sinks
options.D: Standard black plastic waste bins

explanation: Sharps must go directly into rigid, puncture-resistant containers to prevent accidental needle pricks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: A patient with a history of asthma is admitted for post-abortion care. What is your most important first step?

options.A: Discharging the patient with an inhaler
options.B: Starting intravenous antibiotic therapy
options.C: Establishing accurate baseline vital signs
options.D: Restricting all oral fluids immediately

explanation: Getting accurate baseline vitals gives you a starting point so you can quickly spot any sudden changes in breathing or circulation.

question: Which medication is most commonly given to newborns right after birth to prevent eye infections?

options.A: Erythromycin 0.5% ophthalmic ointment
options.B: Hydrocortisone anti-inflammatory cream
options.C: Silver nitrate solution ten percent
options.D: Normal saline irrigation drops

explanation: Great job! Erythromycin ointment is the go-to choice in the delivery room because it safely stops gonococcal infections without causing heavy irritation.

question: What must you always check before involving a partner or family member in a PAC patient's care plan?

options.A: The explicit consent and permission of the client
options.B: Mandatory attendance at a community health seminar
options.C: A written approval letter from the hospital administrator
options.D: Proof of legal marriage verified by hospital registration

explanation: The patient's privacy is paramount. You can never bring family or partners into her care without her clear go-ahead.

question: Why are waste handlers considered a high-risk group for unsafe injection practices?

options.A: They frequently handle poorly disposed sharp medical waste
options.B: They process expired oral medications in the pharmacy
options.C: They administer injections to community members at home
options.D: They clean hospital floors without wearing heavy boots

explanation: Waste handlers often encounter stray needles thrown into regular trash instead of puncture-proof safety boxes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h4)

question: What triggers the strong inflammatory flare-up called the Mazzotti reaction during parasite treatment?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the plastic pill capsule
options.B: Sudden dehydration caused by lack of drinking water
options.C: Direct toxic injury to human liver cells by the drug
options.D: The rapid release of proteins from dying microfilariae

explanation: You're doing great! When masses of tiny parasites die off all at once, releasing their proteins into the blood, it sparks a strong immune reaction.

question: Why do nurses use tools like the Perceived Stress Scale during patient assessments?

options.A: To replace physical examinations and vital signs
options.B: To measure the patient's exact blood cortisol levels
options.C: To diagnose specific psychiatric disorders definitively
options.D: To quantify the patient's subjective feelings of stress

explanation: Everyone feels stress differently. These scales help nurses turn a patient's personal feeling of overwhelm into clear information so they can give the best care.

question: In public health nursing, how do we look at a "community"?

options.A: A static collection of buildings and roads managed by local government
options.B: A strict political boundary with no movement of people across borders
options.C: A group of patients admitted to the same hospital ward at one time
options.D: A dynamic social system with interacting individuals sharing common interests

explanation: Think of a community as a living network of people who affect and support each other—not just houses on a map!

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) in the hospital?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside nursing care with automated robots
options.B: To store a digital version of a patient's medical history and chart
options.C: To publish patient health data on public internet search engines
options.D: To track financial profits and billing for insurance companies

explanation: An EMR is simply the digital upgrade to old paper folders. It keeps all of a patient's history neatly in one place so your team can access it easily!

question: What is the primary makeup of a Parent-Teacher Association?

options.A: Parents, guardians, and school teachers
options.B: Medical doctors and community nurses
options.C: Government officials and local chiefs only
options.D: Senior secondary school students

explanation: The PTA is specifically formed by the people directly responsible for raising and educating the children at home and in school. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why do nurses give routine immunizations to patients?

options.A: To stimulate adaptive immunity and build long-term memory cells
options.B: To instantly kill any bacteria currently residing in the bloodstream
options.C: To trigger an immediate innate response via localized vasodilation
options.D: To replace missing white blood cells in immunosuppressed clients

explanation: You're doing great! Vaccines give a safe preview of a germ so your adaptive system can build memory cells for future protection.

question: Which hormones primarily drive the physical changes of puberty?

options.A: Thyroid hormones and cortisol
options.B: Growth hormone and melatonin
options.C: Estrogens and testosterones
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: Sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone are the main chemical drivers of pubertal development. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe nursing practice when dealing with antagonistic medications?

options.A: Observing the patient for expected therapeutic reversal of toxicity
options.B: Checking full medication lists for accidental drug cancellations
options.C: Ignoring herbal remedies because they do not interact with hospital drugs
options.D: Understanding whether an antagonist is competitive or non-competitive

explanation: Never ignore herbal supplements! Many herbs can mess with hospital medications through unexpected chemical or drug interactions. Always check the full list!

question: Which lifestyle habit directly damages blood vessels and is a major cause of sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Cigarette smoking
options.B: Eating fresh green vegetables
options.C: Walking briskly every morning
options.D: Drinking too much clean water

explanation: Smoking harms blood vessel walls and reduces blood flow all over the body, which heavily impacts sexual function.

question: What happens to the color absorption properties of hemoglobin when it binds with oxygen?

options.A: It absorbs more red light and less infrared light
options.B: It absorbs more infrared light and less red light
options.C: It turns the surrounding plasma completely dark blue
options.D: It stops absorbing all types of light completely

explanation: Oxygenated hemoglobin absorbs infrared light differently than deoxygenated hemoglobin, which allows the oximeter sensor to measure the ratio. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of a multidisciplinary team approach in maternal health?

options.A: It reduces the total number of healthcare facilities needed in a state
options.B: It ensures that only doctors make clinical decisions for patients
options.C: It eliminates the need for any documentation or record keeping
options.D: It combines different professional skills to ensure a safe continuum of care

explanation: Working together allows various cadres to pool their unique skills, supporting the mother effectively across all stages of care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h3)

question: How should a nurse first care for an exposed spinal sac on a newborn with spina bifida cystica?

options.A: Leave it wide open to the air to dry out
options.B: Apply tight plaster bandages over the area
options.C: Wash the nerves gently with antiseptic soap
options.D: Apply a sterile, moist saline dressing and keep baby off their back

explanation: We want to keep that delicate tissue moist and safe from infection, while making sure the baby lies on their side or tummy so there's no pressure on the sac.

question: What is a common behavioral sign that someone might be struggling with drug abuse?

options.A: Consistent attendance at routine clinical check-ups
options.B: Sleeping uninterrupted for eight hours each night
options.C: Sudden personality changes and withdrawal from family activities
options.D: Eating balanced meals at regular hours every single day

explanation: Watch out for secrecy, sudden mood swings, and a person pulling away from family and friends. You're learning to spot the clinical signs!

question: When should you NEVER perform routine eye irrigation?

options.A: Mild redness caused by ordinary environmental dust
options.B: A suspected penetrating injury or rupture of the eyeball
options.C: A chemical splash involving standard household bleach
options.D: A small speck of sand trapped under the lower eyelid

explanation: Remember: if the eyeball itself is cut open or ruptured, pushing fluid in will raise pressure and push the inside out. Always check for a puncture first!

question: Roughly what percentage of breast milk is composed of water?

options.A: 99 percent
options.B: 70 percent
options.C: 88 percent
options.D: 50 percent

explanation: Breast milk is mostly water, which is why keeping hydrated is so important for the nursing mother's fluid balance. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h5)

question: During wound healing, which cell type rushes in to build new collagen and repair the tissue matrix?

options.A: Keratinocytes
options.B: Mast cells
options.C: Melanocytes
options.D: Fibroblasts

explanation: Fibroblasts are the master builders of healing skin! They migrate into wounds during the repair phase to pump out fresh collagen and rebuild the tissue.

question: Which type of tummy pain is usually dull, aching, and hard to point to with just one finger?

options.A: Somatic pain
options.B: Visceral pain
options.C: Cutaneous pain
options.D: Neuropathic pain

explanation: When hollow organs stretch or cramp, they cause visceral pain. Because internal organs have fewer pain nerve endings, patients struggle to point to the exact spot.

question: Which common health condition is most directly managed by cutting down on salty foods?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Hypertension
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Type 1 Diabetes

explanation: Spot on! Too much salt makes the body hold onto water, driving up blood pressure. Lowering sodium is key for our patients with hypertension.

question: What is a key informant interview?

options.A: A rigid questionnaire filled out by every single child in the village
options.B: A discussion with community leaders who possess deep local knowledge
options.C: A secret examination taken by nursing students before clinical posting
options.D: A laboratory test used to diagnose stubborn bacterial infections

explanation: Key informants include respected local figures like elders or teachers who can explain community habits and history. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the role of the falx cerebri inside the skull?

options.A: It separates the left and right cerebral hemispheres.
options.B: It separates the cerebrum from the cerebellum below.
options.C: It forms a tight seal to prevent any blood from entering the brain.
options.D: It produces the cerebrospinal fluid found in the ventricles.

explanation: Great job! The falx cerebri is a fold of the dura mater that dips right down the middle to divide the left and right halves of your brain.

question: What are the two best ways to identify a patient before giving them medication?

options.A: Checking the ID band and asking their name and date of birth
options.B: Looking at the room number and asking the hospital cleaner
options.C: Checking the chart stored outside on the nurses' station desk
options.D: Recognizing their face from walking past their bed yesterday

explanation: Always use two unique identifiers—like checking their wristband and asking them to speak their name and DOB—to keep medication mix-ups away.

question: Serum sickness is a classic example of which type of hypersensitivity reaction?

options.A: Type I hypersensitivity
options.B: Type II hypersensitivity
options.C: Type IV hypersensitivity
options.D: Type III hypersensitivity

explanation: You've got this! Serum sickness is a type III reaction that happens when immune complexes build up in the body.

question: What does the French (Fr) scale tell you about a urinary catheter?

options.A: The outer diameter of the catheter tube
options.B: The maximum volume of the retention balloon
options.C: The total length of the drainage tubing
options.D: The rigidity of the catheter material

explanation: Think of the French size as the thickness of the tube. The bigger the number, the wider the catheter!

question: What is the main goal of giving psychological first aid to an abuse survivor?

options.A: Prescribing antidepressant medications to cure trauma permanently
options.B: Offering immediate comfort, safety, and supportive listening
options.C: Forcing the survivor to report the incident to the police
options.D: Conducting deep psychoanalysis of childhood experiences

explanation: Spot on! Psychological first aid is all about offering a comforting presence, meeting basic needs, and easing shock without pushing unwanted counseling.

question: Which skin sign is most often seen in patients with a low platelet count (thrombocytopenia)?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.B: Severe dry and peeling patches
options.C: Petechiae and easy bruising
options.D: Widespread painful blistering

explanation: Without enough platelets to patch tiny leaks in blood vessels, patients easily get tiny red dots (petechiae) and bruises from minor bumps.

question: What is the normal baseline range for a baby's heart rate during labor?

options.A: 110 to 160 beats per minute
options.B: 80 to 100 beats per minute
options.C: 170 to 200 beats per minute
options.D: 60 to 90 beats per minute

explanation: Great recall! A healthy baseline fetal heart rate sits nicely between 110 and 160 beats per minute.

question: A surgical ward is over budget mostly because staff are working too much overtime. What should the nurse manager do first?

options.A: Refuse to admit any new patients until the end of the fiscal year.
options.B: Transfer all experienced senior nurses to outpatient administrative desks.
options.C: Immediately stop purchasing all sterile surgical gloves and basic dressings.
options.D: Evaluate current staffing patterns and optimize scheduling to cover shifts efficiently.

explanation: Smart scheduling fixes the root of the problem! Fixing how shifts are covered stops excessive overtime without cutting corners on patient safety.

question: A researcher groups hospital nurses into junior, senior, and management ranks, then picks randomly from each group. What method is this?

options.A: Systematic sampling
options.B: Convenience sampling
options.C: Stratified random sampling
options.D: Cluster sampling

explanation: Correct! When you divide people into subgroups (strata) first, you ensure every important level is fairly represented in your study.

question: Which of these should you NEVER do when handling hospital disinfectants?

options.A: Disposing of expired chemical solutions safely according to policy
options.B: Guessing the dilution ratio without reading the manufacturer instructions
options.C: Following hospital guidelines for surface cleaning and equipment processing
options.D: Respecting the exact contact time required for the specific product

explanation: Exactly! Never guess dilutions. If you mix chemicals too weak, they won't kill germs; too strong, and they can harm someone. Always check the label!

question: Which body part connects the back of the nose and mouth to the voice box (larynx)?

options.A: Bronchus
options.B: Trachea
options.C: Alveoli
options.D: Pharynx

explanation: The pharynx is simply the muscular tube right behind your mouth and nasal cavity that acts as a highway, guiding air down toward your larynx and lungs.

question: What is the main reason for setting clear, measurable goals in a health plan?

options.A: To give nursing students extra homework assignments
options.B: To prevent community members from asking questions
options.C: To fulfill a strict rule just so salaries get paid
options.D: To know exactly what change is expected and when it should happen

explanation: That's correct! Clear goals give everyone a clear target and a timeline so you can easily tell if your program is working.

question: A patient undergoing fertility testing shares that she feels deeply sad and worthless. What is the best first thing for a nurse to do?

options.A: Assure her that medical treatments work on the first try for almost everyone
options.B: Tell her that adoption is a very easy alternative to consider right away
options.C: Advise her to stop thinking about pregnancy so her hormones will normalize
options.D: Acknowledge her emotional pain and offer a supportive, non-judgmental space to talk

explanation: You nailed it! Validating her deep emotional pain builds essential trust and shows true compassionate nursing care. Keep up the wonderful work!

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for gastric lavage?

options.A: Consuming a small amount of liquid plant fertilizer
options.B: Ingestion of strong corrosive alkali acids
options.C: A mild overdose of over-the-counter paracetamol
options.D: Swallowing a non-toxic household plastic toy

explanation: Corrosive substances severely damage tissue, meaning the mechanical friction of a lavage tube can easily cause an esophageal or gastric perforation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h2)

question: Why do doctors prescribe oral contraceptive pills to women with symptomatic uterine fibroids if they don't actually make the fibroids disappear?

options.A: To replace the need for all future surgical diagnostic evaluations
options.B: To permanently correct the congenital origin of the muscular growth
options.C: To help control heavy menstrual bleeding and reduce pain, even though they do not remove the fibroid
options.D: To permanently dissolve the fibroid tissue within a few weeks of treatment

explanation: You got it! While pills won't cure or shrink the fibroid permanently, they are fantastic for managing heavy bleeding and painful cramps in the meantime.

question: A patient refuses a bath because the bathroom feels cold and confusing. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Scold the patient for being uncooperative with personal hygiene
options.B: Cancel all future baths indefinitely to avoid upsetting the patient
options.C: Warm the room, simplify the process, and break it down into gentle steps
options.D: Force the patient into the tub immediately to maintain hygiene standards

explanation: Making the environment cozy and taking things slow helps ease fear and resistance during personal care.

question: Which sign is a classic clue of right-sided heart congestion?

options.A: Complete loss of vision in both eyes
options.B: Sudden wheezing and frothy pink sputum
options.C: Severe sharp chest pain radiating to the jaw
options.D: Peripheral edema and jugular venous distension

explanation: When the right side backs up, blood dams up in the body's veins. This leads to swollen ankles (edema) and bulging neck veins (jugular venous distension).

question: How does the sympathetic nervous system affect your digestion?

options.A: It speeds up peristalsis throughout the small and large intestines
options.B: It stimulates the release of bile from the gallbladder
options.C: It increases the production of gastric acid and digestive enzymes
options.D: It inhibits digestive activity during times of stress or danger

explanation: Think of the 'fight or flight' response: when you're stressed or running late for class, your body shifts blood away from your gut, slowing down digestion so you can focus on surviving! You've got this.

question: Why does long-term low blood oxygen sometimes lead to secondary polycythemia?

options.A: The liver releases clotting factors to repair damaged alveolar walls
options.B: The bone marrow responds to inflammation by producing excess white blood cells
options.C: The body tries to carry more oxygen by making extra red blood cells
options.D: Dehydrated blood vessels concentrate the existing red blood cells rapidly

explanation: You're nailing this! Making extra red blood cells is the body's clever way of packing more oxygen-carriers into the blood when air supply is low. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h7)

question: During a Gomco clamp procedure, what is the main job of the metal bell component?

options.A: To protect the underlying glans penis from injury during excision
options.B: To deliver continuous local anesthesia throughout the operation
options.C: To hold the urinary catheter securely inside the bladder
options.D: To measure the exact length of the penile shaft

explanation: The metal bell acts like a shield, fitting right over the sensitive glans to keep it safe from the scalpel and the tight clamp.

question: As a nurse, what is the most important check you must do before giving a patient a new antibacterial drug?

options.A: Testing the patient's visual acuity
options.B: Weighing the patient on a digital scale
options.C: Checking the patient's allergy history
options.D: Measuring the patient's abdominal girth

explanation: Safety first! Always check for allergies so you don't trigger a severe, life-threatening reaction like anaphylaxis.
